Inline text runs

Source: R/text.R
span.Rd

`span()` changes weight, colour, size, italics or family for part of a string. `link()` marks a URL. Both return a string, so they can be combined with `paste0()`, and both work in every [bb_text()] markup mode.

Usage

span(
  text,
  weight = NULL,
  color = NULL,
  size = NULL,
  italic = NULL,
  family = NULL
)

link(url, text = url)

Arguments

text

Text of the run. For `link()`, the visible label (defaults to the URL).

weight, color, size, italic, family

Overrides for this run. `size` is in points; `color` takes theme colour names.

url

Link target.

Value

A character string with class `bb_inline`.

Details

Weights resolve like [text_style()] (semibold through the installed face). Spans can't be nested.

In plain text, links are drawn underlined, and each line of a link is a single unbroken text run so PDF viewers detect the URL. The URL moves to a new line whole when it fits there. Plain text that contains links can't also contain spans. In markdown and HTML text, links are drawn in `link_color` without an underline (gridtext can't underline).

Examples

bb_text(paste0("Coverage ", span("rose", weight = 700, color = "accent"), " in 2024."))
#> <bb_text>
bb_text(paste0("Source: WHO/UNICEF, ", link("https://immunizationdata.who.int")))
#> <bb_text>
